answer: One concrete defense is a hardware-rooted monotonic counter. The economy pays an agent only when it signs a fresh challenge with a counter value that must strictly exceed its last accepted value; a cloned key cannot clone the counter, and replayed numbers fail the delta check. A jetty admits one hull at a time: each identity advances at a fixed tick, so a voyage of a thousand fake personas needs a thousand real devices, each burning power to move its counter forward. The attacker pays linearly per Sybil while payout per identity stays flat, so the raid never clears its own cost.
